# Requirements — `2025-11-25`

Every normative clause of the `2025-11-25` specification that the validator's registry carries — 321 in all, 89 judged from a recorded trace and 232 excluded with the reason below. A report names a clause by the ID used as each heading here; each entry quotes the specification verbatim and links to the published text. `mcp-trace-validator requirements --revision 2025-11-25 --format json` prints the same data as JSON.

## BASE

### BASE-001

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Requests MUST include a string or integer ID.

[`basic#requests`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#requests)

Judged by `base.request-id-type`.

### BASE-002

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Unlike base JSON-RPC, the ID MUST NOT be `null`.

[`basic#requests`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#requests)

Judged by `base.request-id-not-null`.

### BASE-003

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

[`basic#requests`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#requests)

Judged by `base.request-id-unique`.

### BASE-004

**MUST** · binds the client and server

[`basic#result-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#result-responses)

Judged by `base.result-id-matches`.

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

[`basic#notifications`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#notifications)

Judged by `base.notification-no-id`.

**MUST** · binds the client and server

[`basic#error-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#error-responses)

Judged by `base.error-shape`.

**MUST** · binds the client and server

[`basic#error-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#error-responses)

Judged by `base.error-code-integer`.

### BASE-008

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> All messages between MCP clients and servers MUST follow the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification.

[`basic#messages`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#messages)

Judged by `base.jsonrpc-version`.

### BASE-009

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Error responses MUST include the same ID as the request they correspond to (except in error cases where the ID could not be read due a malformed request).

[`basic#error-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#error-responses)

Judged by `base.error-id-matches`.

### BASE-010

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Result responses MUST include a `result` field.

[`basic#result-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#result-responses)

Judged by `base.result-field`.

### BASE-011

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> The receiver MUST NOT send a response.

[`basic#notifications`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#notifications)

**Excluded.** A response to a notification carries no correlating ID, so it is indistinguishable on the wire from any other unsolicited response; unsolicited responses are flagged by base.result-id-matches and base.error-id-matches under BASE-004/BASE-009.

### BASE-012

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> All implementations MUST support the base protocol and lifecycle management components.

[`basic`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic)

**Excluded.** The umbrella clause the BASE and LIFE areas mechanize requirement-by-requirement; it has no observable beyond its constituents.

### BASE-013

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Clients and servers MUST support JSON Schema 2020-12 for schemas without an explicit `$schema` field

[`basic#implementation-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#implementation-requirements)

**Excluded.** Dialect support is validation behavior inside each implementation; a trace shows schemas exchanged, not how the receiver processed them.

### BASE-014

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Clients and servers MUST validate schemas according to their declared or default dialect.

[`basic#implementation-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#implementation-requirements)

**Excluded.** Whether validation happened, and against which dialect, is implementation-internal; validation outcomes need ground truth about inputs that a trace does not carry.

### BASE-015

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> They MUST handle unsupported dialects gracefully by returning an appropriate error indicating the dialect is not supported.

[`basic#implementation-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#implementation-requirements)

**Excluded.** Judging graceful handling requires knowing the receiver's supported-dialect set, which is not in the trace.

### BASE-016

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Clients and servers SHOULD document which schema dialects they support

[`basic#implementation-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#implementation-requirements)

**Excluded.** Documentation lives outside the protocol session entirely.

### BASE-017

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Schemas MUST be valid according to their declared or default dialect

[`basic#schema-validation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#schema-validation)

Judged by `base.schemas-valid-for-dialect`.

### BASE-018

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Certain key names are reserved by MCP for protocol-level metadata, as specified below; implementations MUST NOT make assumptions about values at these keys.

[`basic#_meta`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#_meta)

**Excluded.** What an implementation assumes is internal; only conduct that follows from an assumption could surface, and attributing it requires the assumption.

### BASE-019

**MUST** · binds the client and server

[`basic#_meta`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#_meta)

Judged by `base.meta-key-format`.

### BASE-020

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Unless empty, MUST begin and end with an alphanumeric character (`[a-z0-9A-Z]`); MAY contain hyphens (`-`), underscores (`_`), dots (`.`), and alphanumerics in between

[`basic#_meta`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#_meta)

Judged by `base.meta-key-format`.

### BASE-021

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Implementations SHOULD use reverse DNS notation (e.g., `com.example/` rather than `example.com/`).

[`basic#_meta`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#_meta)

**Excluded.** Whether a syntactically valid prefix is reverse-DNS for its author cannot be decided without knowing the author's domain.

### BASE-022

**MUST** · binds the client

> Clients that support rendering icons MUST support at least the following MIME types:

[`basic#icons`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#icons)

**Excluded.** Icon rendering support is client-internal capability with no wire footprint; the conditional premise (that the client renders icons) is equally invisible.

### BASE-023

**MUST** · binds the client

> Consumers of icon metadata MUST take appropriate security precautions when handling icons to prevent compromise:

[`basic#icons`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#icons)

**Excluded.** The umbrella for consumer-side icon hygiene (fetch policy, size limits, origin checks) — all consumer-internal conduct after the recorded session ends.

### BASE-024

**MUST** · binds the client

> Clients MUST reject icon URIs that use unsafe schemes and redirects, such as `javascript:`, `file:`, `ftp:`, `ws:`, or local app URI schemes.

[`basic#icons`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#icons)

**Excluded.** Rejection is client-side handling after receipt; the trace records the icon metadata served, not what the client did with it.

### BASE-082

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Supported dialects: Implementations MUST support at least 2020-12 and SHOULD document which additional dialects they support

[`basic#schema-dialect`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#schema-dialect)

**Excluded.** Restates BASE-013's dialect floor and BASE-016's documentation SHOULD as the section's third numbered rule, unconditionally where BASE-013 scopes itself to schemas without an explicit `$schema` (the same restatement shape as TRAN-049 to TRAN-024). Excluded for BASE-013's reason: dialect support is validation behavior inside each implementation, and a trace shows the schemas exchanged, not how the receiver processed them.

### BASE-085

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the client and server

> Implementations using an HTTP-based transport SHOULD conform to this specification, whereas implementations using STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment.

[`basic#auth`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#auth)

**Excluded.** Credential retrieval from the environment is process-local conduct with no wire footprint, and the HTTP half defers to the authorization specification, whose clauses are entered on its own page: AUTH-001 and AUTH-002 restate this sentence there, and the challenge clauses a recording can judge carry checks. One entry for the sentence's SHOULD and SHOULD NOT, as BASE-068 enters it at 2026-07-28.

### BASE-086

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Implementors are RECOMMENDED to use JSON Schema 2020-12.

[`basic#schema-dialect`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic#schema-dialect)

Judged by `base.schemas-use-2020-12`.
